verdict: Jacobs' gross revenue jumped 34% to $4.08B — flattered by pass-through project costs and the PA Consulting acquisition — while its cleaner 'adjusted net revenue' grew 8% and a temporarily high tax rate cut GAAP EPS to $1.16.

segments.name: Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities
segments.note: Engineering and building data centers, semiconductor plants, energy, water and transport projects. Of its $3.75B gross revenue, $1.66B is pass-through costs billed to clients, leaving $2.09B of adjusted net revenue, up 10%.

segments.name: PA Consulting
segments.note: The innovation and technology consultancy Jacobs acquired — its first full quarters inside the group.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Bidding for work, running projects' back office and corporate costs — including about $21M of charges tied to the PA Consulting transaction and the separation program.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $55M, partly offset by $8M of interest income and $1M of miscellaneous income.

takeaways.title: Record backlog
takeaways.text: Backlog hit a record $28.9B, up 27%, with a trailing book-to-bill of 1.4x — the AI build-out (data centers, chips, power, water) is filling the order book.

takeaways.title: Tax ate the profit growth
takeaways.text: Operating profit rose 22%, but a temporarily elevated 43% tax rate — a side effect of the PA Consulting deal structure — left GAAP net earnings of $137M, down from $181M a year ago.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised again
takeaways.text: Jacobs raised its FY26 adjusted EPS and net revenue guidance midpoints for the third consecutive quarter, and bought back $142M of stock in the quarter.

oneTimers: The quarter's 43% effective tax rate was temporarily elevated by the PA Consulting acquisition transaction — the main reason GAAP earnings fell despite higher operating profit.
SG&A includes roughly $14M of restructuring charges for the PA Consulting transaction and $8M for the separation program.
footerNote: Jacobs reports 'gross revenue' including $1.66B of pass-through costs it bills to clients; its preferred measure, adjusted net revenue, was $2.42B. Page figures follow GAAP gross revenue. Jacobs' next quarter (Q4 FY26) had not been reported when this page was built. Amounts rounded to $M; direct costs and PA Consulting revenue absorb $1M rounding differences so the lines add exactly.
